title: From Quaternionic Spacetime to MOND: A Single ε Anchored to H₀ Links Galaxies and Cosmology
content: The multimessenger bound on the speed of gravitational waves (|c_T / c – 1| ≲ 10⁻¹⁵) imposes a stringent filter on modified gravity theories. We present the first phenomenological test of a PT-symmetric quaternionic (PTQ) framework, in which luminal tensor propagation (c_T = 1) emerges as a structural consequence of the underlying symmetries, rather than from parameter tuning. In the weak-field limit, this framework produces a one-parameter dictionary that links cosmology and galaxy kinematics via a single, global, dimensionless parameter epsilon. This parameter leads to three key predictions: (1) it sets the MOND acceleration scale as a_0 = epsilon × c × H_0; (2) it attributes the diversity of galaxy rotation curves to a predictable, geometry-only efficiency factor kappa ≈ average(h/r); and (3) it unifies the cosmological parameter Omega_Lambda and the galactic acceleration parameter a_0. These predictions are tested using a full-likelihood analysis of the SPARC galaxy sample. Our results show that the PTQ model statistically outperforms standard MOND (with a ΔBIC of approximately 38). The geometric nature of kappa is further validated through a novel thickness test, revealing a strong correlation (R² ≈ 0.818) between the inferred kappa, disk thickness, and surface density. Finally, we demonstrate that kappa enables a consistent cross-scale link between cosmological and galactic determinations of epsilon. Altogether, the PTQ framework emerges as a predictive, testable, and empirically successful model that resolves the apparent tension between galactic dynamics and gravitational wave constraints.
